name: The Forger's Call
genre: 1980s Stadium Hard Rock / 1986 Archival Garage Demo / Collegiate Football Anthem
description: Released on CPI Homecoming Weekend (October 15, 2016) as a bonus archival companion disc inside the Live at the Crucible 30th-Anniversary Box Set at The Foundry (and available for purchase separately), The Forger's Call brings the two original October 1986 studio and cassette recordings of 'Ignition: The Forger's Call' to an album for the very first time in history: Track 1 ('Ignition: The Forger's Call', 4:34)—the finished 1986 stadium master blasted over The Crucible PA system at every CPI Forgers home football game as the team runs out of the tunnel onto the field, whose heavy 82 BPM kick drum inspired the student section in The Anvil to organically craft 'The Stomp'—and Track 2 ('Ignition: The Forger's Call (Demo Take 3)', 4:32)—the raw 4-track Tascam Portastudio cassette demo recorded in the unheated garage at 412 Progress Street NE and submitted to the October 1986 CPI student anthem contest, where the band members vocalize 'TING... BOOM!' on the tape to test where the foundry anvil strikes.
subtitle: 30th-Anniversary Archival Companion Release (1986–2016) • Included in the Live at the Crucible Box Set & Sold Separately
linerNotes: For thirty years—from October 18, 1986 until Homecoming Weekend on October 15, 2016—the only way on Earth to hear 'Ignition: The Forger's Call' was to walk through the limestone gates of The Crucible in Blacksburg, Virginia on a Saturday afternoon in autumn. Under the historic $1.00 Perpetual Mutual Cross-License ('The Progress Street Redline') drafted at the kitchen table of 412 Progress Street NE by sixteen-year-old dual-enrolled prodigy Holly O'Connell, the band intentionally kept 'Ignition' off every studio album, compilation, and commercial release for three decades so that it belonged exclusively to Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) and the sixty-five thousand fans inside The Crucible.

To celebrate the 30th Anniversary of 'Ignition: The Forger's Call' alongside the release of Live at the Crucible (where the band and the 300-piece CPI Marching Forgers opened the May 21, 2016 concert with the song's first-ever live album performance), Engine Room Records opened the Blacksburg vault to release The Forger's Call—included as a bonus companion disc inside the Live at the Crucible 30th-Anniversary Box Set at The Foundry (CPI's campus bookstore) and also available separately.

This archival companion release pairs both historic October 1986 recordings side by side for the first time: Track 1 ('Ignition: The Forger's Call') is the official 1986 Crucible Stadium Master played over the stadium PA towers before kickoff at every CPI Forgers home football game as the football team charges out of the tunnel onto the field—featuring a real steel foundry anvil strike and Tyler Wright's chest-rattling 82 BPM kick-drum groove to which the student section in The Anvil organically invented 'The Stomp' over several successive plays. Track 2 ('Ignition: The Forger's Call [Demo Take 3]') is the original Maxell XLII-S 90 4-track cassette tape submitted to the October 1986 CPI Student Government Association contest, preserving 22-year-old Ryan O'Connell's garage studio slate to Holly and the band members vocalizing 'TING... BOOM!' on the tape to test the idea of where the anvil strikes.

studioArchives.title: Track 1: The 1986 Crucible Stadium Master & The Organic Birth of "The Stomp"
studioArchives.content: When the Progress Street cassette demo won the October 1986 student contest, Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler tracked the finished 82 BPM stadium master ('Ignition: The Forger's Call') specifically for the press-box audio booth at The Crucible. Replacing their garage vocal placeholders with an authentic steel foundry anvil strike and Tyler's booming kick drum, this is the song the CPI Forgers football team runs out onto the field to at every home game. The band never wrote a stomp into the lyrics—instead, over several successive Saturdays in The Anvil, the CPI student section organically began stomping the galvanized steel bleachers in unison on Tyler's heavy 82 BPM kick-drum hits, creating a 126.2 dBA seismic roar that registers on the Copernicus Hall seismographs and allows every Forger (including wheelchair users locking their brakes and slamming their footplates or fists on the kick drum) to shake the earth of Blacksburg together.

studioArchives.title: Track 2: "Demo Take 3" — Vocalizing "TING... BOOM!" in the Progress Street Garage
studioArchives.content: Recorded in October 1986 on a 4-track Tascam Portastudio cassette deck inside the unheated two-car garage at 412 Progress Street NE, 'Ignition: The Forger's Call (Demo Take 3)' is the exact cassette tape that won the CPI student contest. Because the five college kids didn't have a real blacksmith's anvil in the garage yet, Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler vocalized 'TING... BOOM!' directly onto the 4-track tape to test where the anvil chime and bass-drum boom would land.

studioArchives.title: The 1986 $1.00 Perpetual Mutual Cross-License ("The Progress Street Redline")
studioArchives.content: Before handing 'Demo Take 3' to the CPI Student Government Association in October 1986, 16-year-old Holly O'Connell crossed out the university's boilerplate Work-for-Hire clause in red ink and negotiated a $1.00 Perpetual Mutual Cross-License with CPI's Office of University Counsel. In exchange for CPI's perpetual, royalty-free right to blast 'Ignition: The Forger's Call' at all home athletic events and perform it with the 300-piece Marching Forgers, the band kept 100% of their master and publishing rights and secured a perpetual license to reference CPI, The Forgers, and The Crucible across their catalog.
